findings.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:291 — Light- and dark-theme color values are reversed, reducing link contrast in both themes.
app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss:522 — `.name` incorrectly uses 50% in both themes instead of 30% for light and 70% for dark, making it indistinguishable from `.title`.
app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss:497 — Mobile `.name` incorrectly uses 50% in both themes instead of 30% for light and 70% for dark, collapsing the name/title hierarchy.
app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102 — `.custom-message-length` has swapped theme values, using 30% for light and 70% for dark instead of 70% and 30%, contradicting the desktop rule.
app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:182 — `h3` incorrectly uses 50% in both themes instead of 20% for light and 80% for dark, weakening contrast and making it identical to `h4`.

goldens.comment: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion

This change for desktop/user.css changes $primary from 30% to 50% for the light theme; most other changes preserve the original $primary value and move the complement to $secondary for dark. Consider reviewing this (also applies to a similar .name change in the mobile variant).
In topic-post.css the original code used $lightness: 70% but the replacement uses $lightness: 30% for the light theme. This makes the text significantly darker than intended.

The light theme color for `.topic-meta-data h5 a` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, which may unintentionally reduce contrast and affect readability. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with design intentions.
In mobile/user.scss line 497, the lightness value for dark themes should be inverted to 70% instead of being changed to 50%. This change may lead to unintended visual regressions in light themes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102 — `.custom-message-length` has swapped theme values, using 30% for light and 70% for dark instead of 70% and 30%, contradicting the desktop rule.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies an inconsistency. In mobile/modal.scss line 102, the change is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. In desktop/modal.scss line 50, the equivalent rule uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. The mobile version has the lightness values swapped (30%/70% vs 70%/30%), which would produce different visual results between desktop and mobile for the same element. This appears to be a bug where the values were accidentally reversed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:182 — `h3` incorrectly uses 50% in both themes instead of 20% for light and 80% for dark, weakening contrast and making it identical to `h4`.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss around line 179-182, the h3 element is changed from `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The finding correctly identifies that this uses 50% lightness for both light and dark themes, whereas the original was 20% lightness. Looking at h4 at line 187, it also uses 50%/50%. The pattern elsewhere in the codebase (e.g., desktop/topic-post.scss line 318) shows h3 should use 20%/80% for proper contrast hierarchy. This appears to be an inconsistency/error where h3 was changed to match h4's styling instead of maintaining the contrast difference.
